claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: maxUnavailable 'specifies the maximum number of Pods that can be unavailable during the update process... issues.quote: For the two api Pods, the Deployment turns these limits into one extra Pod at a time and none missing: the diagram's five steps.
issues.text: Both limits are 'about a quarter', yet one becomes 1 and the other 0. The sentence now tells me the Deployment does this, so I can accept 1 and 0 as facts and follow the diagram, but I still paused on why the same 25% gives different numbers.
issues.fix: Add a short clause after 'none missing' telling the reader that how the Deployment turns a percentage into whole Pods is not covered here, so the asymmetry reads as intended, not as a typo.

issues.quote: With no extra checks in this manifest, a Pod is available as soon as it is ready, so the script's `ready` and section 4's "available" mean the same here.
issues.text: Section 4 says a Pod is available once its container is running; this says available once ready. I had to re-read both to conclude running, ready and available all coincide here. 'extra checks' and section 4's 'a check of whether the api can actually serve' also look like two different things.
issues.fix: Replace 'With no extra checks in this manifest' with 'With no check of whether the api can serve, as in section 4,' so both sentences name the same missing check.

issues.quote: right after `apply` in step 3 answers `configured`, the watch of step 2 still shows Pods on the ReplicaSet being replaced, for a few more seconds.
issues.text: The watch prints ReplicaSet rows with numbers, not Pods. I understood it, but I had to work out that 'shows Pods on' means the `1.0.0` row still has DESIRED or READY above 0.
issues.fix: Replace 'still shows Pods on the ReplicaSet being replaced' with 'still prints new rows in which the `1.0.0` ReplicaSet has READY above 0'.

issues.quote: the `DESIRED` of the two ReplicaSets changes one Pod at a time, the `sha-` one going up as the `1.0.0` one goes down.
issues.text: The watch in step 2 has no `-o wide`, so it shows no IMAGES column. To tell which row is the `sha-` one I must match names against step 1's output, which the lesson does not say; I could also infer it from which row starts at 0.
issues.fix: Add one clause: 'the `sha-` one is the row that starts at 0, the name step 1 listed with the `sha-` image'.
